text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Nigeria's economy is bouncing back and should be completely out of the "woods" next year, says chairman of federal revenue board James Naiyeju.
- Nigeria's renowed social science professor Claude Ake was among others on list of passengers on crashed plane.
- Except for kids who roamed the streets and soldiers on patrol volatile Ogoniland was calm on Sunday during first anniversary of hanging of Ogoni minority rights activists.
- Manufacturers Association of Nigeria proposes measures for next year's fiscal budget to stimulate economic growth.
- Poland to invest in Nigerian coal industry and reactivate dillapidated mines, says Polish embassy's commercial counsellor Jan Padlewski at Lagos international trade fair.
- More oil marketing forms announce dismal profits, the latest being African Petroleum.
